Author: tholin
Content: Even if you got those high speed interfaces on a gf180 chip, there is nothing you can put on that chip to generate or process data at those speeds.

Author: tholin
Content: WCH makes a chip that is a PCIe to RS232 adapter (just a PCIe version of their popular USBTTL chips). If you put that on a board with a gf180mcu SoC and set it to one of the higher supported UART rates, i.e. 500000bps, you’d have all the throughput you need.

Author: tholin
Content: To share my personal experience: I taped out a RISC-V core on GFMPW-1, about as performant as a non-pipelined core could get, and wired it up to a SPI <-> 10/100mbps ethernet bridge (enc28j60) and the system kept dropping packets because the RISC-V CPU struggled to process them faster than they were coming in.

Author: tholin
Content: Like, it’d frequently die during IPv6 SLAAC or IPv4 DHCP because the broadcast responses combined with background broadcast traffic on my home network overflowed the buffer.

Author: tholin
Content: So, 10/100mbps ethernet on gf180mcu would make sense, but then you’re hitting data processing speed limits anyways.

Author: rebelmike
Content:
I don’t think I’ve even pushed the repo to GitHub yet. But the main things I’ve done:
Use FemtoRV as the core.
2 clocks per instruction for all instructions except memory access and branches. Predictable performance in general to allow cycle counting. No C extension.
Add some B extension instructions. In particular I found rotates being missing a problem when writing for BIO as it meant you couldn’t easily shift bits out to an arbitrary pin. Bit and byte reverse. And the logical ops with one inverted operand.

Author: rebelmike
Content: One note, so far this is a rewrite. I haven’t been referencing the original BIO implementation, just the spec. But also I haven’t got as far as doing the FIFOs yet - I’ve just got GPIO working on a single core. So possibly this would be a good point to try and transplant what I have into the original BIO implementation, especially if this project might be gaining a deadline.
